title: r1 W1 fix incomplete: the nudge-skipped timeline line still ships an implementer-authored em-dash, and the claimed no_em_dash_test extension never landed
evidence: r1's own codebase lens flagged this exact line at 9d66ce9 (r1 codebase.c1.json finding #2: "copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail (renders 'Applicant nudge skipped — {detail}')"). The rework (167a43b) fixed only the consts (`refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed` is now "Applicant nudge: couldn't send", copy.gleam:825 — no dash) but left the skipped arm unchanged at e0f9fa7, reference_panel.gleam:632-634: `copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail` (const at copy.gleam:823 = "Applicant nudge skipped"). The composed line renders e.g. "Applicant nudge skipped — co-nudge skipped: form already opened" — the em-dash joins the internal sweep gate-skip reasons verbatim (server/src/reference_checks/sweep.gleam:376-377: "co-nudge skipped: form already opened" / "co-nudge skipped: draft exists"). UX §7.6's timeline ships em-dashes only on the "label — channels" join ("Invitation sent — email + SMS"); no nudge step has one, and this line is implementer-authored (r1 codebase lens already ruled the batch_line " — " join at reference_panel.gleam:624 fine for mirroring §7.6). Additionally the W1 fix map's second half — "no_em_dash_test extended to scan refcheck consts" — did NOT land: client/test/copy_test.gleam:308-312 `no_em_dash_test` still iterates `for_each_copy` (toast/page codes only, copy_test.gleam:298-306), diff.c2 touches only client_test.gleam and reference_panel_test.gleam, and no test scans refcheck copy for the dash. The composed string evades any pin.
detail: Per the r2 fix-audit mandate, a missing/wrong fix is a finding at the r1 severity (W1 = warning). The banned character still ships in a landlord-visible timeline line that fires in production whenever the T+24h co-nudge is gate-skipped (form opened or draft exists — a normal state), and the raw internal reason text is duplicated in the label ("nudge skipped — co-nudge skipped: ..."). The ban-test extension the fix map claims is absent, so CI cannot catch a reintroduction.
recommended_fix: Drop the em-dash from the skipped line (e.g. "Applicant nudge skipped. " <> detail or a plain space), and extend no_em_dash_test (or a panel-copy sweep) to scan the refcheck_* constants and the composed timeline labels. Consider mapping the internal skip reasons to landlord-facing copy instead of rendering "co-nudge skipped: form already opened" verbatim.

title: Off state still renders the panel heading "Reference Checks (0)" and the §7.8 explainer, whose copy is factually false when the feature is off
evidence: view() renders `view_explainer(explainer_open, app.first_name)` unconditionally (reference_panel.gleam:84) — only the sub-line is suppressed for `off` (line 80-83). With off=True, the card therefore shows "Reference Checks (0)" (refcheck_heading(list.length(calls)), calls=[] — FR-RC3 suppresses row creation on declined attestation) plus the collapsed "What this tells you" toggle above the §7.4 Off block. The explainer body (copy.gleam:543-560) states "A completed reference means the person at the contact details {name} gave confirmed the facts shown... References here are collected in writing (a secure form). Nobody is called, and nothing is recorded." — claims the Off state can never deliver (no references are ever collected when the applicant declined). §7.4's Off block spec is heading + body + referee contact chips only; §7.3 describes the explainer as panel chrome for the checking flow. The off_state test (reference_panel_test.gleam:595-613) asserts no re-ask and no rows but does not pin the explainer's presence/absence, so the mismatch is unpinned either way.
detail: A landlord in the Off state is offered an explainer whose sentences describe completed written references — misleading given the applicant declined automated contact. Low impact (collapsed by default) but it is the panel's own honesty rule violated in the Off branch.
recommended_fix: Hide the explainer (and arguably the heading) when off=True, or amend the copy so the Off state's explainer does not promise completed-reference semantics.

title: Panel-test fixtures still use the phantom wire value "their_landlord" that r1 W2 was about — the render-level tests never exercise the real "landlord" value
evidence: completed_result() (line 111) and the partial fixture (line 428) both embed `"relationship_to_applicant":"their_landlord"` — the phantom value r1 W2 flagged (the server stores "landlord": server/src/reference_checks/questions.gleam:125 `#("landlord", form_copy.opt_their_landlord)`, read back via result.gleam:170). The fix correctly mapped "landlord" -> "Their landlord" in copy.gleam (refcheck_choice_word) and dropped the defensive "their_landlord" key, so `refcheck_choice_word("their_landlord")` falls through `_ -> value` and renders raw. No assertion in reference_received_state_test (line 380) or partial_state_test (line 426) checks the Relationship cell, so the raw phantom value sits in the serialized HTML unnoticed, and no component-level render test exercises the real wire value end-to-end (only the word-map unit tests choice_word_map_is_total_test / choice_word_map_resolves_landlord_relationship_test do).
detail: The fixtures mimic a payload the v1 server can never emit for this question, so the summary-render path for the landlord-relationship word is only pinned at the word-map level. A regression in how the Relationship row renders the real "landlord" value would pass CI. Cosmetic today, but it is precisely the gap that let W2 ship in r1.
recommended_fix: Change the two fixtures to "landlord" so the render tests exercise the real wire value, and optionally pin the Relationship cell text ("Their landlord") in reference_received_state_test.
